To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

yoghurt made from buffalo milk with 3% culture, 13.5% total solids, nil UF retentates and heated to 85 ° C/30 min resulted in significantly better sensory and rheological parameters and shelf life of 2 weeks at 4 ° C.
yoghurt prepared from buffalo milk using 2.5% culture, 13.75%, 0% UF retentate, 13.5% total solids and 80 °C/30 min heat treatment was found to be the best among all the treatments.   1
the addition of ultrafiltered retentates adversely affected the quality parameters of yoghurts.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an optimised process for the manufacture of plain set yoghurts from buffalo milk with a shelf life up to 15 days.
the effect of UF retentate on the physicochemical, rheological and sensory properties of buffalo milk plain yoghurt.
the improvement of quality of buffalo milk yoghurt by optimization of culture level, UF retentate level, total solid level and heat treatment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of UF retentate for the preparation of plain set yoghurts should be avoided.

the quality of buffalo milk plain yoghurt was improved by optimization of culture levels and total milk solids, and heat treatment at 85 °C for 30 min, whereas the quality was deteriorated by the addition of ultrafiltered retentates.
UF retentate adversely affected the sensory quality of yoghurt, whereas optimization of process parameters improved the sensory quality of plain set buffalo milk yoghurt.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
UF retentate should not be added to the milk for making yoghurt.
the quality of plain yoghurt made from buffalo milk can be significantly improved by optimizing the process variables.

the yoghurts prepared by using 13.5% total solids, 2.75% culture level, 80 °C/30 min heating of milk, and nil UF retentates addition was found to have the highest overall acceptability score (7.3), and was significantly better than the control sample and the market sample (7.1 and 5.7 respectively).
The main takeaway from our work is that
buffalo milk yoghurt can be made of high quality with an optimised culture level, total milk solids, UF retentate and heat treatment.
the addition of UF retentate to buffalo milk for the production of plain set yoghurts is not advisable.
the quality of buffalo yoghurt could be improved through optimization of the culture, total milk solids and UF retentate levels, and heat treatment.
